item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I can’t in good faith upvote or no vote this piece. The prose feels cluttered and overused, the character himself comes across as silly and hammy- but my biggest critique is just that this isn’t anything new.

I don’t expect an AWCY article to reach philosophical enlightenment, but at its very core this piece boils down to ‘modern art is getting a bit out of hand, right guys?’, and that really leaves a sour taste in my mouth. I enjoy all walks of art and media so perhaps there’s a bias at play, but that exact same observation has been made a thousand times. It’s not particularly exciting and the prose isn’t anything to write home about. As such, my verdict is a definite -1.

item.title: I like its simplicity. It's a story!
item.content:encoded:
I like its simplicity. It tells a story in a few paragraphs, which is well done and difficult to do, and many pieces can often be three times this length and say less than a third of what this is saying. It is a criticism of the current state of AWCY, in the same campy language exactly as you would expect from art descriptions. It captures the prose really well as expected from an overdramatic description of one's own art.

Here's a description of Rothko, aka, 'the guy that paints fuzzy rectangles'.

One of the pioneers of Color Field Painting, Rothko’s abstract arrangements of shapes, ranging from the slightly surreal biomorphic ones in his early works to the dark squares and rectangles in later years, are intended to evoke the metaphysical through viewers’ communion with the canvas in a controlled setting.

I would argue that potentially the descriptions of ideas and arts that the artist was trying to convey should be a lot more evocative than they are now. There's a moment where you can reference other AWCY articles in the most exaggerated, over-the-top description possible, like the author is not only critiquing the AWCY world but is calling out other AWCY creators.

item.content:encoded:
now my question is should I keep this article up for context or let the readers know just by the tale?

In general I advise against self-deleting. If it comes down by standard process, well that's just how she goes sometimes; and this discussion thread might pick up more useful feedback you can use in the time it takes for that to happen.

In the process of writing the tale you might find yourself revising the details of the art installation that the story revolves around, and end up with a rewritten version of this GOI-Format that will stand solidly as it's own seperate article. Or you may simply fold the entire idea into one piece. It'll just take the time and effort of trying different things and getting feedback on what works or what doesn't.

For the record, I've decided to give an upvote here for the thought-provoking concept. Though I reckon I might like it better if the article itself did a bit more of the legwork on exploring that concept. Good luck with your follow-up efforts!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I… am having a hard time pinning down just how I feel about this article.

Like others, I can see the parrallels it seems to draw with 'contemporary art' in the real world. If one looks, they can find plenty of debate on the talent / skill / creative merits of certain artworks or art forms; if they deserve to be called "art"; ultimately on what even is our definition of art. I think it's an interesting question, without necessarily any one correct answer.

But I reckon it's that line of thinking, of those questions raised, that might be the best part of the concept. I'll second the notion that maybe a tale would let you explore the angles more expansively, and likely be more directly engaging to the reader.

Though, one could argue that if this piece incites such thought and deep reflection in its audience then it is indeed high art… Hmmm, think I'll take a little time and a re-read before voting.

item.title: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
I expected people not to like this article honestly because of how dumb the concept is, so fair deuce.

The idea behind this is a joke about how something that can blend in so well it stands out, so I mainly took the "irony" bit of it and turned it into the most pretentious thing I can write. I genuinely don't have a point aside from that base concept.

My main issue with this article is that it feels contrarian for the purpose of being contrarian. There's no real larger point to it all except "normal is abnormal" - which, while correct in this context, doesn't do anything for me.

My secondary problem is that the prose feels off in a way that I can't really pinpoint. A good chunk of it is definitely due to the shortness of the article - there isn't enough time for me to really get invested in this proposal or whoever it is that's proposing it. However, at the same time, it also feels overstretched - the core idea is too simple to elaborate on without repeating yourself and using fluff (the abstract section highlights this issue well; you're placing too much emphasis on stuff that the reader would be able to infer even if the bench was anomalous in some way).
